ORIGINAL PHENOMENON CONTEXT:
Track interacting excitatory and inhibitory neural-population activities in a recurrent circuit after a fixed perturbation. Excitatory recurrence recruits additional activity, whereas delayed inhibitory feedback suppresses excitation and can generate damped or sustained rhythmic population dynamics. Both population activities are evolved from initial conditions through bounded neural recruitment and relaxation. The target is the instantaneous derivative of excitatory population activity.

CURRENT EQUATION:
  dE_dt = ((1 - E)/(1 + exp(-(gain_E/(1 + shunt_SI_E*S_I))*(w_EE*E - w_EI*I + external_drive_E - threshold_E - threshold_shift_SI_E*S_I/(1 + sat_threshold_SI_E*S_I)))) - E)/tau_E - g_IE_delayed*S_I*E

CURRENT SYMBOLS (symbol [role] — description):

  t [V] — time
  E [S] — Normalized activity of the excitatory neural population
  I [S] — Normalized activity of the inhibitory neural population
  S_I [S] — Delayed inhibitory synaptic gating or inhibitory trace acting on the excitatory population
  tau_E [P] — Positive effective excitatory-population relaxation time scale
  tau_I [P] — Positive effective inhibitory-population relaxation time scale
  tau_SI [P] — Positive relaxation time scale for inhibitory synaptic gating
  w_EE [P] — Nonnegative recurrent excitatory coupling strength
  w_EI [P] — Nonnegative inhibitory-to-excitatory feedback strength
  w_IE [P] — Nonnegative excitatory-to-inhibitory recruitment strength
  external_drive_E [P] — Constant external drive to the excitatory population
  external_drive_I [P] — Constant external drive to the inhibitory population
  gain_E [P] — Positive gain of the excitatory recruitment response
  gain_I [P] — Positive gain of the inhibitory recruitment response
  threshold_E [P] — Excitatory recruitment threshold at zero inhibitory threshold shift
  threshold_I [P] — Inhibitory recruitment threshold
  g_IE_delayed [P] — Strength of delayed inhibitory synaptic suppression onto excitation
  shunt_SI_E [P] — Strength of inhibitory shunting or divisive gain reduction of excitatory recruitment by inhibitory trace
  threshold_shift_SI_E [P] — Strength by which inhibitory trace raises the effective excitatory recruitment threshold | suggested range: nonnegative; often 0 to order-one relative to threshold_E or external drive scale
  sat_threshold_SI_E [P] — Saturation strength limiting further inhibitory threshold displacement at large inhibitory trace | suggested range: nonnegative; often 0 to moderate so that 1 + sat_threshold_SI_E*S_I stays positive and threshold displacement saturates over the admissible S_I range

(a) constant renaming or merging, e.g. k*x -> (k+a)*x with fixed k and a;

cannot activate under the scenario's admissible conditions;
(c) a promoted quantity that remains constant in the intended experiment;
(d) a correction expected to be negligible throughout the admissible domain;
(e) only changing auxiliary trajectories while leaving the scored mapping from
supplied observations unchanged, e.g. making dv/dt complex when scoring dx/dt=v
and v is supplied. Prefer another scientifically justified gap when one of
these applies. Do not select a redundant change just to fill a generation slot.

response relationship, e.g. temperature-dependent stiffness with varying T;
parameter changes are not forbidden as a category.
